quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Keep more distance between you and the car ahead.
Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
Use your horn only when there is an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving it on confuses other drivers about which direction you are going.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go slowly and be careful.
Turn around and take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What colors should motorcycle riders wear to be more visible?

options.text: Brown, gold, silver, and white
Blue, black, gray, and purple
Orange, red, yellow, and green

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange, red, yellow, and green
questions.explanation: Bright orange, red, yellow, and green are the best colors for motorcycle riders. These bright colors make it easier for other drivers to see you on the road.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle footrests?

options.text: The driver and passenger can share the same footrests.
Footrests are required for both the driver and passenger.
Footrests are not required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Footrests are required for both the driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Both the driver and passenger must have footrests and keep their feet firmly on them for balance. This keeps your passenger from falling off and pulling you off too.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or when visibility is poor.
Always use your headlight.
Put an orange tint on your headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Using your headlight at all times is the single best thing you can do to help other drivers see your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding during the day?

options.text: Brightly-colored clothing so others can see you better.
Clothing of any color because it is easy to see during daylight.
Dark-colored clothing to stand out against the bright sun.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brightly-colored clothing so others can see you better.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Always wear bright clothing to make yourself more visible, even during the day.

questions.question: What is the best way for a group of motorcycles to ride together?

options.text: One behind the other in a single line.
In pairs side by side.
In a staggered pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered pattern.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group of motorcycles to stay together while giving each rider enough space to ride safely.

questions.question: If a driver makes eye contact with you, does it mean they see you?

options.text: Yes, they have definitely seen you.
Not always. They may look at you but not actually notice you.
Yes, and they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not always. They may look at you but not actually notice you.
questions.explanation: Never assume a driver has seen you just because they made eye contact. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but fail to actually see them.

questions.question: What should happen when you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go first.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: This is a traffic regulation sign. It has white background with red and black markings. This sign tells you that right turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger should:

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle stops.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: The best way to handle someone tailgating you is to:

options.text: Get off the road.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let tailgaters pass. Speeding up only increases danger by causing them to continue tailgating at the higher speed.

questions.question: Stopping while turning is difficult because:

options.text: The bike is leaning, so less traction is available for stopping.
The rider is focused on the turn, not on braking.
The brakes do not work while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bike is leaning, so less traction is available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but it requires care. When the motorcycle leans for a turn, some traction is used for turning. This leaves less traction for stopping.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should generally be in:

options.text: A single-file line.
Pairs.
A staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group to stay close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, entering a highway, or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When entering a turn, the best time to change gears is:

options.text: Before the turn.
During the turn.
While in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before entering a turn. If you must change gears during a turn, do it smoothly.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked until your next stop.
Continue squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure. Then immediately re-apply pressure with controlled, gradual pressure.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Provide you with an escape route.
Expose you to wind blasts.
Show other drivers your intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expose you to wind blasts.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should protect you from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use only your front brake.
Use only your rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply controlled pressure to both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Avoid sudden moves because they can cause a skid.
Travel on the shoulder to stay away from traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake does not work on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves because they can cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, any sudden change in speed or direction can cause a skid. Be smooth when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.
